curriculum.course_title: New York State Next Generation Mathematics Learning Standards (2017, updated June 2019), Grades 1-5

source_notes: Extracted programmatically from the official NYSED P-12 standards PDF; two-column layout interleaves statements with marginalia, so statement text and cluster headings are best-effort pending Standards Mapping review.
Coherence chains are official vertical-alignment content published inside the document and are preserved per-row.
NY identifiers are jurisdiction-native (NY- / AI- / AII- / GEO- prefixes); they must never be merged with CCSS identifiers from other states' inventories by similarity.
New York has no repository packs, seeds, or skills; every row is NO_REPOSITORY_SPECIFIC_MAPPING_FOUND pending Standards Mapping work.

Recognize a square with side length 1 unit, called “a unit square,” is said to have “one square unit” of area, and can be used to measure area. b. Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling it, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths. b. Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning. c. Use tiling to show in a concrete case that the area of a rectangle with whole-number side length a and side length b + c is the sum of a × b and a × c.
